newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Big trade in Leplats ahead of mines merger.
newsitem.headline: Big trade in Leplats ahead of mines merger.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd (Leplat), which is to merge with fellow mining firms in the Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) stable, dipped in heavy trade on Monday.
Dealers said that most of the more than three million shares that changed hands did so in a single bookover deal, where a broker acts as both a buyer and seller of shares.
"The volumes are big, but the value is not. The interest may be on the the merger. We should hear soon from Anglo how the merger will work," a dealer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.
Martindale Stacey Du Toit Inc, the brokerage that did the deal, declined to comment.

Amplats, the world's largest platinum producer, said earlier this month it would combine itself and its three listed mining firms -- Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (Rusplat), Leplat and Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd (PP Rust).
Analysts have said that the merger will fortify Amplats for the future and enable it to optimise a united cash base and shared ore reserves.
It was this future strength that made it possible for the platinum producer to plan for a big new mine and expand existing operations.

Amplats has announced that it will develop a new 1.2 billion rand mine at Boschkoppie and expand PP Rust's concentrator. This will see about 250,000 ounces of newly-mined platinum being produced with full production reached in 2002.
Dealers said the four cent slip in Leplat's share price on Monday to leave it at 286 cents by 1330 GMT came on the back of a weaker platinum price.
"Platinum stocks are all easier for choice on the metal price," one said.
Platinum was last trading at $386.50/387.50 an ounce from a previous London fix on $387.50.
